layers.title: The Root
layers.subtitle: What this Name means linguistically
layers.content:
The Name Al-Haadi (الهَادِي)

The Guide

This Name appears among the 99 Names of Allah in the hadith of the Prophet: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' (Sahih Muslim)
layers.quran_ref: Quran 22:54 — Indeed Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet said: Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise. — Sahih Muslim
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: The Meaning
layers.subtitle: The full understanding of this Name
layers.content: The Guide — the one who guides whomever He wills from among His servants to the straight path, the one who places guidance in the heart. No one finds guidance except through Him — and He guides only those who sincerely seek it.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 22:54 — Indeed Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: In the Quran
layers.subtitle: Where Allah calls Himself by this Name
layers.content:
Allah calls Himself Al-Haadi in the Quran. The placement of each Name is not accidental. When Allah ends a verse with Al-Haadi, He is signalling that the meaning of that Name is the reason for what preceded.

Quran 22:54 — Indeed Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path

The scholars note that knowing which Name closes which verse deepens understanding of the Quran itself. The Name is the key to the verse.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 22:54 — Indeed Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: The Scholar
layers.subtitle: Ibn Uthaymeen's explanation
layers.content:
Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen (rahimahullah) taught that the Name Al-Haadi must be understood in its full depth:

The Guide — the one who guides whomever He wills from among His servants to the straight path, the one who places guidance in the heart. No one finds guidance except through Him — and He guides only those who sincerely seek it.

He emphasised that truly knowing the Names of Allah changes a person — not merely memorising them, but understanding their meaning and living in light of them. He who knows Allah as Al-Haadi will relate to Allah differently, supplicate to Him differently, and trust in Him differently.
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: Your Reflection
layers.subtitle: What this Name means for your life
layers.content:
The Name Al-Haadi is not only something to know about Allah — it is something to live in relation to.

The Prophet said: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' The word for enumerate — ahsaha — means to know, understand, act upon, and call upon Allah by each Name appropriately.

Reflect: When do you most need to call upon Allah as Al-Haadi? What situation in your life right now makes this particular Name the one you need most?

The Quran says: 'And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them.' (7:180)
layers.quran_ref: Quran 7:180 — And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them
layers.hadith_ref: Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise — Sahih Muslim
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

quiz.prompt: What is the primary meaning of the Name Al-Haadi?

options.text: The Guide
The All-Knowing
The Most Powerful
The Creator

quiz.citation: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Name Al-Haadi means the guide. Knowing the precise meaning allows you to call upon Allah by this Name at exactly the right moment.

quiz.prompt: How many Names does Allah have according to the hadith?

options.text: One hundred names
Ninety-nine — one hundred less one
Seventy-two names
An unlimited number

quiz.citation: Sahih Muslim — Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one
quiz.scholar_reflection: The scholars note Allah has more Names than ninety-nine — these are the specific Names He has revealed. The ninety-nine are a door; what lies beyond is immeasurable.

quiz.prompt: In which Quranic context does the Name Al-Haadi appear?

options.text: Quran 22:54 — Indeed Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path
Quran 1:1 — Ar-Rahman, Ar-Raheem
Quran 112:1 — Al-Ahad
Quran 2:255 — The Throne Verse

quiz.citation: Quran 22:54 — Indeed Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path
quiz.scholar_reflection: Allah places each Name in a specific context. He is telling you through the Name He chose why He did what He did. The Name is the key to the verse.

quiz.prompt: What does truly 'enumerating' the Names mean according to the scholars?

options.text: Memorising them in Arabic
Knowing, understanding, acting upon, and calling upon Allah by each Name
Counting them on prayer beads
Writing them in calligraphy

quiz.citation: Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: Memorisation is only the beginning. Call upon Al-Mujeeb when you need response, Al-Ghafoor when you need forgiveness, Al-Lateef when you need subtle help.

quiz.prompt: What does the Quran command regarding the Names of Allah?

options.text: Memorise them all
Call upon Him by them
Recite them after every prayer
Teach them to your children

quiz.citation: Quran 7:180 — And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them
quiz.scholar_reflection: The purpose of knowing the Names is calling upon Allah by them — in du'a, in dhikr, in trusting Him. Knowledge that does not change how you relate to Allah has not fully entered the heart.

quiz.prompt: Allah is Al-Haadi — the guide. When have you most needed Him to be this for you?
quiz.slider_label: How often do you call upon Allah by this specific Name?

options.text: In a moment of fear or danger
When I needed something no one else could provide
When I felt broken or ashamed
I have not thought about needing this quality specifically

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Names of Allah become real in the moments we need them most. Each Name is a door — and Allah placed exactly this Name in your path at exactly this moment.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet said whoever enumerates the Names enters paradise. What is the relationship between truly knowing Allah and the Garden?
quiz.slider_label: How much does your knowledge of Allah shape your daily choices?

options.text: Knowing Who Allah truly is makes it impossible to live as if He does not exist
The Names change how you relate to Allah in every act of worship
Understanding the Names removes the distance between you and Him
All of these — true knowledge of Allah transforms everything

quiz.citation: Sahih Muslim — the hadith of the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: You do not enter paradise by reciting a list. You enter because true knowledge of Allah reshapes who you are — your love, your fear, your trust, your worship.

quiz.prompt: Allah is Al-Haadi. How does knowing this change how you make du'a?
quiz.slider_label: How specific are you when you call upon Allah?

options.text: I call upon Him by this Name when I need what it describes
I have not thought about matching the Name to the need
It makes me more confident that my du'a will be heard
It makes me more specific and sincere in asking

quiz.citation: Quran 7:180 — Call upon Allah by His Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: Calling upon Al-Ghafoor for forgiveness is not the same as calling upon Al-Qadir for strength. Match the Name to the need — this is what the Quran commands.

quiz.prompt: Ibn al-Qayyim said the heart is created to love something. What makes Allah the most worthy of that love?
quiz.slider_label: How much of your relationship with Allah is based on knowing Who He is?

options.text: He is the source of every good thing you have ever received
He loves you even when you are heedless of Him
He is Al-Jameel — beautiful — and beauty draws love
All of these — each Name reveals another reason to love Him

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Names of Allah, when truly known, make Him the most worthy object of love. The more Names you know, the more of Him you know — and the more of Him you know, the more naturally the heart turns toward Him.

quiz.prompt: If you spent one week consciously remembering that Allah is Al-Haadi, what would change?
quiz.slider_label: How present is awareness of Allah in your daily life?

options.text: My anxiety would decrease — I would trust more completely
My du'a would become more sincere and specific
I would act differently knowing He is aware of everything
I would feel less alone in whatever I am facing

quiz.citation: Practical reflection on the Name Al-Haadi
quiz.scholar_reflection: The purpose of knowing the Names is taqwa — constant awareness of Allah. Not fear alone, but awareness. When you are aware of Al-Qareeb, you are never truly alone.
